statement_blocker: The repository supplies only an FFT method label and a fast-DFT slogan. It fixes no DFT sign or normalization, input and output carrier, index representation, admissible lengths or factorization, Cooley-Tukey variant, recursion and permutation, executable semantics, correctness relation, termination claim, arithmetic cost model, operation set, or exact/asymptotic complexity conclusion. Choosing a radix-2 O(N log N), mixed-radix, algebraic factorization, or implementation-correctness theorem would invent proposition-changing mathematics.
target_decision: redirect the catalog method label to a corrected, independently reviewed, source-selected exact FFT correctness and/or complexity proposition before ordinary statement or proof execution
domain_and_universes: Open: an accepted source must fix the signal/value carrier, scalar and equality structure, finite index type, transform length and factorization, algorithm state and representation, cost carrier and asymptotic domain, universes, and all typeclass context.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not choose algebraic Cooley-Tukey decomposition, equality of a recursive algorithm with a dense DFT, termination, exact operation count, asymptotic O(N log N), numerical error, or a conjunction of these results.
degenerate_case_status: No boundary case is excluded at intake because no proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve every transform, length, factorization, recursion, permutation, arithmetic, cost, and implementation case listed in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: algebraic Cooley-Tukey factorization of a DFT of composite length N1 * N2

correctness of a mixed-radix decimation-in-time or decimation-in-frequency algorithm
exact complex addition and multiplication count for one selected FFT
asymptotic O(N log N) arithmetic complexity in a selected cost model
floating-point forward or backward error analysis of a selected implementation
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: zero, singleton, prime, composite, and power-of-two transform lengths
factors equal to zero or one, repeated or noncoprime factors, and factor ordering
empty and singleton signals, zero and constant signals, and invalid input lengths
forward versus inverse sign and normalization conventions
decimation-in-time versus decimation-in-frequency and input/output permutation direction
recursion base, empty factorization tree, stride and layout semantics
arithmetic-only versus memory/index/root-generation cost and exact versus asymptotic bounds
exact complex arithmetic versus floating-point, overflow, rounding, and error guarantees
excluded_substitutions: THM-M-0341 Fourier transform inversion, THM-M-0358 Fourier multiplier theorem, or THM-M-1261 Fourier integral operators
the quantum Fourier transform or any quantum circuit theorem
the dense mathematical DFT definition or inversion theorem without a fast algorithm and checked bridge
continuous Fourier transforms, Fourier series, character bases, roots of unity, or convolution alone
an algorithm specialized to a length or convention not accepted by the source-selected root
a structure or hypothesis storing the desired DFT equality, termination, or cost result
